messages:
jamie_support: heads up — ACME Integrations opened a support ticket (S-42178). They say streaming responses are being counted as 5xx when their client times out/disconnects mid-stream. sample request-id: r-0a9f3c. Can eng-sre take a look?

acme_integration: hi team, repro steps: we call your hosted /v1/stream endpoint with chunked encoding and our mobile SDK sometimes drops the socket during long responses. on our side, we see a client disconnect. on your billing dashboard it shows a 5xx for that request. want to avoid being billed for failed responses.

jamie_support: attaching brief logs from their SDK and the gateway trace they provided:

acme_integration: ```
REQUEST r-0a9f3c headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked
body: <prompt tokens>
CLIENT: mobile-sdk v1.2.3 -> connection reset by peer after ~12s
GATEWAY: upstream closed connection, status=502? reason=pipeclose
```

rahul_sre: thanks — quick q: is the gateway labeling final status as 5xx or is the accounting layer mapping half-close events to 5xx? need the exact gateway logs for r-0a9f3c. jamie, can you paste the trace id?

jamie_support: trace attached in the ticket. snippet from gateway: `upstream: write failed: broken pipe while sending chunk`, then `request terminated, status=499` (huh, but billing shows 502).

ana_platform: (actually ana_platform) hmm mixed signals. 499 is client closed request (nginx-style). our billing pipeline historically treated 4xx as non-billable but we added a rule that any stream terminated before final chunk was considered a 5xx for safety. that rule might be over-aggressive.

eva_cs: customer is very sensitive to billing noise — they're already flagged high volume. can we reproduce locally by dropping the socket mid-stream? if so we should update the classification.

rahul_sre: repro plan: spin up the latest gateway image, call /v1/stream with a slow generator so server emits chunks for ~30s, then simulate client FIN (tcp half-close) from client side and observe upstream/gateway logs and final status code. i'll do that and paste logs.

ops-bot: deploy started: gateway/stream-proxy @ sha:ac3f7e (canary) — rahul_sre, note that canary has the streaming heartbeats patch from last week.

rahul_sre: test run results: reproduced. sequence: server sent chunk 1..n, client FIN at ~12s, gateway reported `upstream: write failed: EPIPE` then emitted `stream terminated, classification=5xx` in the accounting event. under the hood our stream classifier sees EPIPE and maps to transient upstream failure.

ana_platform: that's the mapping I mentioned — we added that mapping to catch real upstream crashes where kernel returns EPIPE, but it also catches deliberate client disconnects. need to disambiguate.

jamie_support: suggested mitigation for now? customer asked for immediate credit if we decide misclassification.

rahul_sre: short term: add a heuristic — if client TCP FIN arrives within X ms of the last data chunk and there is no upstream error trace (stacktrace, oom, exit), classify as client-abort (499) not 5xx. I'll open a hotfix PR to adjust classification backfill window to 200ms.

ana_platform: long term: we should enrich gateway events with the socket-level closure reason and expose `client_close` vs `upstream_close` flags into the billing pipeline. also add a test that simulates chunked encoding + half-close to prevent regression.

eva_cs: i've told the customer we'll pause billing for affected request-ids while we investigate. please post the list of affected request-ids (r-0a9f3c & r-0b7e2d) and the PR link.

rahul_sre: logging with request-ids: r-0a9f3c, r-0b7e2d, r-0c4a9f. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/pull/4523 — patch changes EPIPE -> consider client FIN detection before mapping to 5xx.

jamie_support: thanks. i'll update the ticket and ask CS to confirm credits. can we get a timeline for hotfix rollout?

rahul_sre: aiming for canary within 2 hours, full deploy in 6-8 hours if no regressions. i'll post back with canary logs.

acme_integration: really appreciate the fast turnaround. once patched, could you also share recommended retry guidance for our SDK? we want to avoid double-charging and minimize duplicate responses.

ana_platform: recommend: treat client disconnect as terminal — don't auto-retry from the client. server-side idempotency token could be used if you need safe retries. we'll also add a header `x-rw-stream-terminated: client_disconnect|upstream_error` in future to help clients decide.

rahul_sre: canary logs: after PR applied, simulated client FIN -> gateway now records `classification=client_abort(499)` and billing event flagged as non-billable. no downstream regressions seen in 1000 synthetic streams.

jamie_support: great — closing loop with ACME. eva_cs, can you confirm crediting and inform customer?

eva_cs: yes, I'll process the credit for the three request ids and send a confirmation email. thanks team :tada:

jamie_support: putting this on the runbook: streaming half-close heuristics, reproduction steps, and the PR link. moving thread to resolved once billing processed.
